model: Qwen2.5-1.5B (GGUF instruct — COST proxy; architecture same as the fine-tuned model)
findings: FP16 (~3.1 GB) did NOT fit on the Orin; INT8 (1.76 GB) and 4-bit (1.04 GB) fit and ran on the GPU.
For classification (single-pass/prefill) INT8 is the sweet spot: both faster (197 vs 211 ms) and lower energy (1374 vs 1607 mJ). 4-bit only saves memory (~40%).

MAXN_SUPER is not the lowest-energy point: at fixed-max clocks power rises while latency stays similar -> energy/sample rises (race-to-idle trade-off). Chosen as a fully defined, reproducible operating point for the paper.
8 GB shared memory: even INT8 fits only after dropping caches (a few ENOMEM).
not: The exact classifier figures will be confirmed with an ONNX exact-model; llama.cpp is a backbone proxy.
